message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations that drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists should know: | Area | Key Points | Practical Tips | |------|------------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• School zones: 20 mph (or 25 mph if posted) during school hours.
• Construction zones: 15 mph or posted speed. | • Always obey posted signs; use your GPS or navigation app to stay aware of speed limit changes. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • Seat belts required for all occupants.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | • Check that every passenger is buckled before you start driving. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held texting or calling while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Install a hands‑free system or use voice‑activated controls. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • If you’re unsure of your BAC, never drive. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have the right of way at crosswalks.
• “Stop” signs require a full stop even if no traffic is present. | • Yield to pedestrians and always come to a complete stop at stop signs. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are only for foggy conditions. | • Keep headlights clean and properly aimed. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Towing requires a valid registration and insurance.
• Vehicles must display a valid license plate on the rear. | • Keep registration documents in the vehicle. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of a driveway or on a sidewalk.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | • Observe all parking signs and use designated spaces. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses automated enforcement cameras in many counties. | • Drive within posted limits to avoid tickets. | | **School Bus Laws** | • All vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• The bus’s red lights and stop sign must be visible. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until the lights are off and the sign is retracted. | | **Cyclist & Pedestrian Laws** | • Cyclists must ride in the same direction as traffic and use hand signals.
• Pedestrians must use crosswalks where available. | • Share the road responsibly; give cyclists and pedestrians ample space. | ### Quick Reference Resources | Resource | What It Offers | How to Access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** | Official traffic laws, road maps, and safety tips | https://www.txdot.gov | | **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC)** | Licensing, registration, and DUI information | https://www.txdmv.gov | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement updates, safety campaigns | https://www.txdps.state.tx.us | | **Texas Traffic Law Handbook** | Comprehensive guide to state traffic statutes | Available at local libraries or online PDF | --- #### Common Mistakes to Avoid 1. **Running Red Lights** – Even if you think you’re clear, the law requires a full stop. 2. **Using a Hand‑Held Phone** – The penalty is a fine plus points on your license. 3. **Failing to Yield to Pedestrians** – Pedestrians always have the right of way at crosswalks. 4. **Driving Without a Valid License Plate** – You can be ticketed and fined. If you need more detailed information on a specific topic (e.g., DUI penalties, toll roads, or commercial vehicle regulations), let me know!
